newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ says interested in Czech Skoda stake.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ says interested in Czech Skoda stake.

text.p: Slovak steel maker VSZ a.s. said on Monday it was currently holding preliminary talks on the possibility of acquiring an undisclosed stake in Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s..

"I have declared a certain interest of VSZ's in Skoda ...certain probing negotiations are ongoing about whether we would get a stake, but I cannot specify the size," VSZ spokesman Jozef Marko told Reuters.
He also declined to provide any other details, adding that VSZ would release an "official statement on the topic" after its board of directors meeting scheduled for early on Tuesday.
A spokesman for Skoda in the southwest city of Plzen said the firm had no knowledge of VSZ's intentions.

Two of Skoda's major shareholders, banks IPB and Komercni Banka -- which hold 5.9 percent and 11.7 percent of Skoda respectively -- declined comment in the Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Monday as to whether they were in talks with VSZ on selling their stakes.
Last week, the Czech government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), said on Wednesday it was planning to sell 8.7 percent stake it holds in Skoda soon.
The NPF said the stake would probably be sold on the capital market within weeks if no property restitution claims appeared which could block it.
Skoda's largest shareholder is NERo s.r.o., owned by Skoda General Director Lubomir Soudek. He has expressed an interest to add the NPF stake to his current 21.5 percent holdings in Skoda.
The company is the largest Czech engineering concern, based in the western city of Plzen. Skoda's production range spreads from beer cans to trucks and nuclear reactors.
It is no longer affiliated with Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s..
VSZ is Slovakia's largest steel maker, employing some 25,000 workers. It has some 100 subsidiaries and holds stakes in firms ranging from banks to airlines to soccer teams.
